item.title: [LU-17296] NRS TBF default rules
item.description:
One issue with Lustre in highly-contended multi-application workloads is the "noisy neighbor" problem, where one application's IO can be negatively affected by another application's IO that is submitted at the same time.

This particularly affects users on login nodes that are trying to run interactive workloads (eg. "ls -l" or compiling applications) that are only submitting a few RPCs at a time, and they can be blocked behind thousands of RPCs from a large job on hundreds of nodes.

It is possible to create NRS TBF rules to limit the RPC processing rate of the servers, but most users do not implement TBF rules, and suffer from this issue.

It would be useful to create a set of default TBF rules that could be applied to all systems, either at installation time or afterward, that provide a "best practice" result for a wide variety of use cases. It should be possible to override the default rules, but for many situations the default should avoid the majority of imbalance between jobs.

For example, applying a very high Token limit (eg. 1M) on jobs by GID, UID, JobID should not constrain the job RPC processing rate if there is no contention, but if there is IO contention on a server then it should fairly balance the RPC rate between the jobs instead of using FIFO order that is often blocking small (eg. interactive user) RPC processing.

Putting in a default JobID rule with a higher TBF allocation for jobs on login nodes (eg. With "*login*" in the job name) would also help boost interactive performance and at least have a reasonable chance of working out of the box. If not, this could be made clear in the documentation to be customized on deployment.

status.description: The issue is open and ready for the assignee to start work on it.

comments.comment: Another option would be to implement the ThemisIO research as a new NRS policy. I asked Opus to design such a thing and it came up with nrs_fairshare.md

hornc, this looks interesting. I would really prefer to have a single NRS policy that implements the various features at the same time (e.g. mostly fairshare, but some specific job or user is limited to a maximum rate, or guaranteed a minimum rate, and ORR sorting is used to improve HDD performance when possible). Having to pick one or the other policy depending on the most important functionality needed makes it complex to configure for users.

It might be that fairshare is better suited to academic, research, "friendly" environments where maximum throughput is the most important, while TBF is better suited to "contentious" environments where tenants (or at least the storage admins) want fixed rates per tenant.

Opus to design such a thing and it came up with nrs_fairshare.md

Could you please put that up on the Lustre wiki (in wiki format) so that it is available for future reference.

I came across a paper AdapTBF_Decentralized_Bandwidth_Control-2026.pdf "AdapTBF: Decentralized Bandwidth Control via Adaptive Token Borrowing for HPC Storage" that implements a dynamically balanced mechanism to provide more balanced IO for jobs.  There isn't a Lustre patch for this today, but I've contacted the authors to see if they have started working on it yet.

I have also read this paper recently. It uses NRS TBF. But I doubt the implementation from the architecture picture: It seems that it uses per-OST TBF to achieve rate control. But in Lustre the NRS TBF is per-service, each service partition can issue I/Os to all OSTs on the OSS node and a OSS server may have multiple OSTs...

> I've contacted the authors to see if they have started working on it yet.
@adilger have they answered?
